Development Phasing:(1) Unless otherwise approved, the phases of the development shall comprise the following:(a) Enabling works;(b) Hard and soft landscape works;(c) Site A (which includes Blocks 1, 2 and 3); and(d) Site B (which includes Block 4).(2) The phases set out in (1) may be commenced sequentially or concurrently as the case may be.Reason: To assist with the identification of each chargeable development ((a) to (d) being each Phase) and the calculation of the amount of CIL payable in accordance with the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended).

Play Space Design:Prior to the commencement of hard and soft landscaping works, details of the play space, including details of equipment and its future maintenance and an implementation timetable, must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The play space must be completed in accordance with the approved details. The play space shall thereafter be permanently retained and kept available for use as play space by occupiers of the development.Reason: To provide a satisfactory quality of play space design appropriate to the requirements of future occupiers.

Materials, Samples and Detailing:Prior to the commencement of above ground building works for each relevant building or phase, the following details for that building or phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:a) External facing materials including sample boards of all facing materials and finishes as well as sample panels of the main brick types;b) Sectional detail drawings at 1:5 (unless otherwise noted below) through all typical external elements/details of the facades including all openings in external walls, doors and window-type reveals, heads and sills;c) Details of junctions between external facing materials;d) Typical details of all balconies;e) Roof details including parapets;f) Plans of ground-floor entrance cores at 1:20, elevations of entrance doors at 1:10 and details of entrance-door thresholds;g) All external metalwork including handrails;h) Details of any external bin storage facilities; andi) Finished floor levels of the ground floor of the building in relation to the adjacent existing and proposed levels;j) details of all walls (including retaining walls), fences, gates or other means of enclosure to be erected in or around the development.The development shall thereafter be carried out solely in accordance with the approved details.Reason: In order to ensure that the building has an acceptable visual impact to the street scene and the surrounding area.

Hard and Soft Landscaping and Public Realm Implementation Plan (Final):Prior to the commencement of hard and soft landscaping works, a scheme of hard and soft landscaping be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme must include:a) An implementation timetable;b) details of trees, shrubs, grass and all other soft landscaped areas;c) street furniture,d) car parking layout, including the location of blue badge, LUL Access Space, car club and service bays and details of how any further spaces for residents' blue badge spaces (up to 35no or 10% provision overall) will be allocated;e) external surfacing materials including sample boards of surfacing materials and finishes as well as sample panels of the main paving types;f) details of a management and maintenance plan for any areas of public realm / landscape; and. g) details and location of water fountain.The scheme shall include the proposed biodiversity enhancement interventions in respect of each phase.Reason: To provide a satisfactory quality of hard and soft landscaping and public realm appropriate to the requirements of future occupiers.

Secure by Design:Prior to first occupation of each block, details shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that relevant block can achieve 'Secured by Design' Accreditation. The development shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved details.The commercial unit hereby permitted shall not be occupied until evidence that it has achieved the relevant Secured by Design certification has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interest of creating safer, and more sustainable communities.

Inclusive Design - M4(2) and M4(3):At least 90% of residential units within the development shall comply with Part M4 (2) 'accessible and adaptable dwellings' of the Building Regulations 2015; and at least 10% of all dwellings hereby approved shall be wheelchair accessible or easily adaptable for wheelchair use (Part M4 (3) 'wheelchair user dwellings' of the Building Regulations 2015).Reason: To ensure inclusive and accessible development.

Sustainable Drainage Strategy including Rainwater Harvesting:Prior to the commencement of development (save for any enabling works), or a relevant phase, a Sustainable Drainage Strategy for that phase must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and must have regard to the approved Preliminary Drainage Strategy. The details shall include:a) Assessment of potential for partial infiltration SuDS, including infiltration testing where appropriate;b) Information on how source control SuDS measures are activated;c) Flow control mechanisms;d) Final sizes, storage volumes, invert levels, cross-sections and specifications of all SuDS measures including green roofs, swales, permeable paving, rain gardens and attenuation features. Include calculations demonstrating functionality where relevante) Final levels plan with overland flow routes identified; andf) A Draft Management Plan for Future Maintenance.A Full Management Plan will be developed and submitted by the contractor prior to occupation. Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development.

Sustainable Drainage Strategy - Verification Report:Prior to the occupation of any phase of the development (save for any enabling works), a Verification Report for that phase demonstrating that the approved drainage / SuDS measures have been fully implemented shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This report must include:a) As built drawings of the sustainable drainage systems including level information (whereappropriate);b) Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systems;c) Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage features; andd) A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similar.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development.

Lighting Details / Plan (Building & Public Realm):No external lighting shall be installed until full details of that external lighting and any other related light sources that may create external light spill have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Each block shall not be occupied until the external lighting in relation to that block has been completed in accordance with the approved lighting details. The external lighting shall thereafter be maintained and retained as approved.Reason: To protect the amenity of local residents and future occupants of the development from undue light spillage and to ensure there are no detrimental biodiversity impacts arising as a result of the development.

Site Management Plan (operational) / Refuse & Recycling Strategy:Prior to first occupation of the development, a Site Management Plan (operational) including a Refuse & Recycling Strategy, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall include:a) Core staff numbers on site at any given time;b) Security provisions on site, if applicable;c) Management of communal areas;d) Refuse and recycling arrangements including disposal details.The development shall not be occupied otherwise than in accordance with the approved Site Management Plan.Reason: To ensure the site is managed in an appropriate way and refuse and recycling is disposed of in a timely and ordered manner, in order to protect the amenity of local residents and future occupiers of the development.

Noise Levels - Construction:No demolition, construction or maintenance activities audible at the façade of any residential dwelling shall be undertaken outside the hours of 08.00 to 18.00 Monday to Friday and 08.00 to 13.00 Saturday or at any time on Sundays and bank or public holidays. Construction work audible at the façade of any residential dwelling may only be undertaken outside of these hours where those works have been approved by the Local Planning Authority under S.61 of the Control of Pollution Act 1974.Deliveries of construction and demolition materials to and from the site by road shall take place between 09:00 - 16:00 Monday to Friday & 08:00 - 13:00 on Saturday and at no other time.The construction activities and construction delivery hours set by this planning condition apply to the works permitted by this Planning Permission only. For the avoidance of doubt, they do not apply to the TfL/LUL Piccadilly Line Upgrade (PLU) works. Reason: To protect the amenity in the locality from undue noise and disturbance.

Noise Mitigation Measures (future occupants):Prior to commencement of above ground works of each block, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating how that block will be appropriately insulated from noise arising from existing nearby noisy uses including the operations of the railway line and underground station. The construction of each block shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure compliance with London Plan (2021) Agent of Change principles and ensure future occupiers of the development are appropriate insulated against noise.

Details of Cycle Parking:Prior to the occupation of the development hereby permitted, details of the provision to be made for cycle parking shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The cycle parking shall thereafter be implemented in full in accordance with the approved details before the use hereby permitted commences and shall thereafter be retained solely for its designated use for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure adequate cycle parking is available on site and to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Delivery and Servicing Management Plan (operational):Prior to the occupation of the development hereby permitted, a Delivery and Servicing Management Plan which shall include details of the location of the service bays shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To protect neighbouring and occupier amenity and ensure there is no traffic congestion resulting from delivery vehicles to and from the site.

Construction Logistics Management Plan (CLMP):Prior to commencement of the development (save for any enabling works excluding demolition), a Construction Logistics Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CLMP shall contain:a) Confirmation of membership of the considerate contractors' scheme;b) Arrangements for wheel cleaning;c) Arrangements for the storage of materials;d) Hours of construction work on site;e) Arrangements for the securing of the site during construction;f) Arrangements for the parking of contractors' vehicles clear of the highway;g) Details of how delivery vehicles will be managed to ensure there is no occurrences of vehicle idling in close proximity to the site;h) Details of how vehicle deliveries will be managed to ensure there is no undue noise anddisturbance to neighbouring occupiers as a result of the deliveries;i) The siting and design of any ancillary structures;j) Arrangements for the loading and unloading of plant and materials;k) Scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works;l) Enclosure hoarding details;m) Procedure for dealing with noise complaints arising from neighbouring occupiers;n) An Air Quality and Dust Management Plan (AQDMP) setting out proposed mitigation measures that will be taken to control dust, noise and other environmental impacts of the development in accordance with the guidance on mitigation measures for Medium Risk sites set out in Appendix 7 of the Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG 2014. Both 'highly recommended' and 'desirable' measures should be included. The AQDMP shall include the following for each relevant phase of work (demolition, earthworks, construction and track out):1) A summary of work to be carried out;2) Proposed haul routes, location of site equipment including supply of water for damping down, source of water, drainage and enclosed areas to prevent contaminated water leaving the site;3) Inventory and timetable of all dust and NOx air pollutant generating activities;4) List of all dust and emission control methods to be employed and how they relate 5) to the Air Quality (Dust) Risk Assessment;6) Details of any fuel stored on-site;7) Details of a trained and responsible person on-site for air quality (with knowledge of pollution monitoring and control methods, and vehicle emissions);8) Summary of monitoring protocols and agreed procedure of notification to the local authority; and9) A log book for action taken in response to incidents or dust-causing episodes and the mitigation measure taken to remedy any harm caused, and measures employed to prevent a similar incident reoccurring.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved CLMP unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the implementation of the development does not lead to damage to the existing highway and to minimise disruption to neighbouring properties and the environment.

Tree Protective Measures / Construction Works within Root Protection Area:Prior to commencement of development (save for any enabling works), a scheme for the protection of retained trees, in accordance with BS5837:2012, including a Tree Protection Plan (TPP) and an Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Specific issues to be dealt with in the TPP and AMS shall comprise:a) Location and installation of services/ utilities/ drainage;b) Methods of demolition within the root protection area (RPA as defined in BS5837:2012) of the retained trees;c) Details of construction within the RPA or that may impact on the retained trees;d) Tree protection during construction indicated on a TPP and construction activities clearly identified as prohibited in this area;e) Boundary treatments within the RPA;f) Methodology and detailed assessment of root pruning;g) Arboricultural supervision; andh) The method of protection for the retained trees.The development thereafter shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details. Should any tree which was identified for retention, be damaged irreversibly it shall be replaced with a tree of equal size and value.Reason: To ensure the retention of and avoidance of damage to retained trees on and off site in the interest of biodiversity, sustainability, and to ensure that a satisfactory standard of visual amenity is provided and maintained.

Contaminated Land - Remediation:(1) Prior to commencement of development (save for any enabling works) a remediation strategy to deal with the risks associated with contamination of each phase shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. This strategy will include the following components: a) A preliminary risk assessment which has identified:i.	all previous usesii.	potential contaminants associated with those usesiii.	a conceptual model of the site indicating sources, pathways and receptorsiv.	potentially unacceptable risks arising from contamination;b) A site investigation scheme, based on (1) to provide information for a detailed assessment of the risk to all receptors that may be affected, including those offsite.c) The results of the site investigation and the detailed risk assessment referred to in (2) and, based on these, an options appraisal and remediation strategy giving full details of the remediation measures required and how they are to be undertaken; andd) A verification plan providing details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy in (3) are complete and identifying any requirements for longer-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action.The scheme shall be implemented as approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by local planning authority.Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to and is not put at unacceptable risk from or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution.

Contaminated Land - Verification:Prior to first occupation of the development, or completion of the landscape works for any phase or part of that may be approved, a verification report demonstrating that the measures set out in the approved remediation strategy have been implemented effectively shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met.If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present no further development shall be carried out until an amendment to the remediation strategy detailing how this unsuspected contamination shall be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete.

Whole Life Carbon: (1) Prior to the occupation of each block, the post-construction tab of the GLA's whole life carbon assessment template should be completed accurately and in its entirety in line with the GLA's Whole Life Carbon Assessment Guidance. The post-construction assessment should provide an update of the information submitted at planning submission stage, including the whole life carbon emission figures for all life-cycle modules based on the actual materials, products and systems used. This should be submitted to the GLA at: ZeroCarbonPlanning@london.gov.uk, along with any supporting evidence as per the guidance. Confirmation of submission to the GLA shall be submitted to the local planning authority, prior to occupation of the relevant block.(2) Unless otherwise agreed, the development shall be implemented in accordance with the postconstruction assessment referred to in paragraph (1).Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to maximise on-site carbon dioxide savings.

Circular Economy:Within 3 months of the first occupation of any of the residential units in the development hereby approved, a post construction statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing to the local planning authority. This shall include the quantification of measures and detail of how circular economy proposals have been achieved in line with approved statement.Reason: To ensure that the proposal promotes circular economy outcomes of the London Plan.

Communal Aerial:Individual aerials shall not be erected across / within the site without consent from the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To protect the character and appearance of the development and the setting of nearby heritage assets.

Digital Connectivity:Prior to the occupation of the development, details of how digital connectivity will be achieved for future residents and occupiers within the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure digital connectivity within the development.

Details of any Rooftop Plant, Extract Ducts and Fans - Acoustic Report (Final):No rooftop plant, or externally facing extract ducts or fans shall be installed until an acoustic report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the combined plant to be installed and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the combined plant does not exceed a level of 10dBA below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest residential property. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance.

Details of any rooftop plant, extract ducts and fans (appearance): Notwithstanding details shown on the submitted drawings, any variations to rooftop plant, extract ducts and fans that would result in a material change to the appearance of the development, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To protect the visual integrity of the development and to ensure the plant extract ducts and fans does not detract from the appearance of the development.

Fire Evacuation Lift (details/management):Prior to the commencement of above ground works for each block, detailed drawings showing fire evacuation lifts in that block shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Each block shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure all future occupiers of the development are able to egress safely and efficiently in the event of an emergency.

Fire Statement:The development shall be carried out in accordance with the measures set out in the approved Fire Safety Statement, unless otherwise agreed with Building Control. The approved measures shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development hereby approved.Reason: In order to provide a safe and secure development.

Electric Vehicles:Prior to occupation of the development, details of electric car charging points shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be occupied until the active electric car charging points have been completed in accordance with the approved details and are available for use.Reason: In the interests of encouraging the use of sustainable methods of transport.

Nesting Boxes:Prior to occupation of the development, details of bird and/or bat nesting boxes/bricks (including their location, number, specification and design of habitats) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so approved prior to the first occupation of the space in which they are contained and shall be retained as such thereafter.Reason: To minimise the impact of the development on the ecological value of the area and to ensure the development provides the maximum possible provision towards the creation of habitats and valuable areas for biodiversity.

Access Demarcation:Prior to commencement of hard and soft landscaping works, details showing clear demarcation between the pedestrian routes and vehicle ways should be provided to improve safety. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: In the interests of improving safety within the Site.

Taxi Stand Details:Prior to the occupation of the development, details of the taxi electric charging bay shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The taxi bay shall not be brought into use until the approved details are available for use.Reason: In the interests of encouraging the use of sustainable methods of transport.

Non-Road Mobile Machinery:No non-road mobile machinery (NRMM) shall be used on the site unless it is compliant with the NRMM Low Emission Zone requirements (or any superseding requirements) and until it has been registered for use on the site on the NRMM register (or any superseding register).Reason: To ensure that air quality is not adversely affected by the development.

Piling Method Statement:No piling shall take place until a Piling Method Statement (detailing the depth and type of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) and piling layout plan including all Thames Water wastewater assets, the local topography and clearance between the face of the pile to the face of a pipe has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority in consultation with Thames Water. Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement and piling layout plan. Reason: The proposed works will be in close proximity to underground sewerage utility infrastructure. Piling has the potential to significantly impact/cause failure of local underground sewerage utility infrastructure.

Green Roof - details:Prior to the occupation of any building or phase of the development, a detailed specification of the green roofs in respect of that building or phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The specification shall include details of the quantity, size, species, position and the proposed time of planting of all elements of the green roof, together with details of their anticipated routine maintenance and protection. The green roofs shall only be installed and thereafter maintained in accordance with the approved details for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In order to introduce high quality soft landscaping in and around the site in the interests of the ecological value of the site and to ensure a satisfactory landscaping of the site in the interests of visual amenity.

Mechanical Ventilation System Details:Prior to the commencement of above ground works, full details (including elevational drawings) of any internal and external plant equipment and trunking, including all building services plant, ventilation and filtration equipment and proposed commercial kitchen exhaust ducting / ventilation, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All flues, ducting and other equipment shall then be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the use commencing on site and shall thereafter be maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure that no nuisance or disturbance is caused to the detriment of the amenities of future residential occupiers or of the area generally.

Water Efficiency - Residential: The residential development hereby approved shall be designed to meet the water consumption target of 105 litres per person per day, with an additional 5 litres per person per day for external water use.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policy SI 5.

Water Efficiency- Commercial: The commercial development hereby approved shall be designed to achieve at least the BREEAM excellent standard for the 'Wat 01' water category160 or equivalent.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policy SI 5.

Construction Hours:No construction involving noisy works audible beyond the boundary of the development site should be undertaken outside the hours of 08:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday and 08:00 to 13:00 on Saturday and at no time on Sunday and Bank Holiday.Reason: in the interests of safeguarding the residential amenities of neighbouring or nearby properties.

Passive House Certification:Prior to the commencement of above-ground works for each residential block, a Passivhaus Strategy Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The report shall be prepared by a Certified Passivhaus Designer or Certifier and shall demonstrate how all residential units within each block will achieve Passivhaus Classic certification. The report shall include:a) Fabric performance specifications, including U-values, window and door performance, thermal bridge treatment, and airtightness targets;b)	Confirmation that the energy strategy for the block complies fully with Passivhaus requirements;c)	Predicted energy demand calculations using PHPP or equivalent accredited methodology;d)	A programme and methodology for achieving certification.Prior to first occupation of each residential block, final Passivhaus certification for that block shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In the event that the final Certificate is delayed due to the independent Passivhaus Certifier timescales, that applicant should submit a Letter of Comfort from the Passivhaus Certifier as sufficient interim evidence to demonstrate that Passivhaus certification can be reasonably expected to be met prior to occupation. The final Certificate will be submitted to the Local Planning Authority once received.  Reason: To secure the delivery of genuinely low-energy homes with assured performance, in accordance with London Plan Policy SI2 and the approved sustainability strategy.

Fuel Poverty / Energy Cost Assessment:Prior to the commencement of above-ground construction works, a Fuel Poverty and Energy Cost Assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The assessment shall:a) Compare projected household energy costs arising from the approved decentralised energy strategy with an alternative scenario involving connection to a district heat network;b) Incorporate current and forecast heat pricing, including pricing data provided by Energetik;c)	Assess the impact on energy affordability across different tenures;d)	Demonstrate how the approved strategy minimises the risk of fuel poverty for future occupants.The development shall thereafter be implemented in accordance with the approved assessment.Reason: To ensure that the proposed energy strategy delivers affordable energy costs for residents and supports fuel poverty reduction, in accordance with London Plan Policy SI2.

Brown Roof and Photovoltaic (PV) Layout Details:Prior to the commencement of above-ground construction works, detailed drawings and specifications shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority showing:a) Confirmation that roofs identified within the approved landscape strategy are delivered as brown roofs;b)	A coordinated brown roof and photovoltaic (PV) layout, demonstrating that available roof space is maximised for PV provision, except where required for access, plant or essential amenity;c)	Details of PV orientation, pitch and coverage.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter.Reason: To secure biodiversity enhancements and maximise on-site renewable energy generation, in accordance with London Plan Policies SI2, G5 and G6.

PV Mounting Method Statement, Maintenance and Energy Management Plan:Prior to the installation of any photovoltaic equipment, a PV Mounting Method Statement, Maintenance and Energy Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The submission shall include:a) Details of PV mounting systems demonstrating that installation will not adversely affect the function or integrity of the brown roofs, including drainage and substrate performance;b)	A long-term inspection, cleaning and maintenance schedule for the PV panels;c)	Details of how electricity generated by the PV array will be utilised on-site, including:i.	Connection arrangements to individual dwellings and/or communal systems;ii.	Calculations demonstrating that on-site consumption is maximised;iii.	Details of any proposed energy storage or PV diverter systems, including diversion to domestic hot water.The approved measures shall be implemented prior to occupation of the relevant dwellings and retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the effective operation, maintenance and on-site utilisation of renewable energy infrastructure while safeguarding biodiversity features, in accordance with London Plan Policies SI2, SI3 and G5.

Parameters:The development hereby approved shall be built in accordance with the approved plans under Condition 2 and be restricted in development quantum to the following: 178 sqm (GIA) of flexible commercial floorspace (Class E and/or drinking establishment (Sui Generis) uses), 715 sqm (GIA) replacement Train Drivers Accommodation (Sui Generis), 373 homes (Use Class C3) comprising of 4 blocks ranging between 6 and 15 storeys above ground level, 4,506 sqm of publicly accessible green space and 386 sqm of residential terrace amenity space.Reason: In the interests of proper planning and for clarity over the development hereby approved.
